steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Flat is easier to read at high zoom.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: No shadows; borders do the work.

steps.use: A strong border and a dimmed page
steps.why: The dimmed page makes the dialog obvious.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge alone, not by its fill.
darkPick: neutral.200: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs in dark, in order to show height by tone,

on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So people see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

pick: shadow.none: We use no shadow for menus and dialogs in order to show their height without a cast shade: the scale gives no layer a step here. The missing shade does this by leaving the layer to its border and the dimmed page behind it. So a dialog stands out at any zoom with no blur to read through, because nothing rises (elevation.roles) and there are no shadows (elevation.values).
darkPick: shadow.none: We use the light pick for the dark overlay elevation in order to keep the height it sets, and the step does this by the same means, so the dark overlay elevation and the light pick never differ, because the step reads the same in dark (theming.values).

steps.rule: The 1px edge of a raised layer. In dark, a solid step lighter than the raised surface, so the edge shows where a shadow cannot.
pick: neutral.200: We use the default line's step for the edge of menus, dialogs and other raised layers, in order to give separation between a layer and what lies under it. The ring does this by a 1px line,

on surface.raised, the layer's only edge, as nothing here casts a shadow. So people see where a menu ends on any page, because raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).
darkPick: neutral.300: We use the step above the raised surface for a 1px ring around raised layers in dark, in order to give separation where a shadow barely shows. The ring does this by a solid, lighter line,

on surface.raised (#595959, no alpha), so its contrast can be checked. So people see a dark menu's edge on any page, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).

pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. The largest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 6px controls inside it. So a step card reads as one object that holds its fields, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is calm and clear (brand.q1).

steps.question: How large is body text?
steps.why: Large text is readable for more people.

steps.question: How big are icons next to text?
steps.why: Larger icons are easier to see.
Large targets help people with motor needs.

darkPick: neutral.600: We use the quietest readable gray for hints and captions in dark in order to keep muted text a step below secondary text (neutral.700). The step does this by reading

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Every state, including loading, gets its own value.
Moderate speed is easy to follow.

steps.use: button/focus-ring at focus.ring.width, with an offset
steps.why: Focus must be seen by everyone.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
darkPick: neutral.50: We use a step darker than content for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets:
on surface.default and
on surface.raised. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads
on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

steps.use: Button secondary, then a confirm page with Button danger
steps.why: A confirm step prevents a costly error.

steps.rule: Real risk: errors, failed checks, actions that cannot be undone. The top of the urgency order. Overuse wears it out.
pick: red.light.700: danger reads as text and icons,
darkPick: red.dark.900: We use the palest red but one for danger in dark in order to keep error labels at
in alerts on content and in destructive menu items, and apart from info for every eye. The step does this by reading
on surface.default and
on surface.raised. Below it, the key (red.dark.600) gives
and red.dark.700

on the raised layer, and red.dark.800 sits within 0.02 of status.info under protanopia. The danger button keeps the key as its fill, and danger text on dark fills is as pale already. So people read an error or a destructive action at full strength in every layer, because text keeps the AAA floor (accessibility.definition) and danger lands in alerts and menus (color.lands).

steps.question: What separates groups on the page?
steps.why: Strong borders separate groups at any zoom.
Space is easy to see; thin lines are not.

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest
, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
darkPick: neutral.300: We use the step above the raised surface for dividers and card borders in dark in order to give separation on every surface a line meets, menus included. The line does this by staying lighter than each surface, lowest
, on surface.raised. So rows and cards stay apart on content and in menus, because lines separate groups (elevation.definition) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).
